note.text: Latitude measures angular position north or south of the Equator. Longitude measures angular position east or west of the Greenwich meridian. Parallels join places of equal latitude; meridians connect the poles. Write latitude first and include the hemisphere. A coordinate without its hemisphere can describe more than one location. Cameroon is in the northern and eastern hemispheres, but classroom points on an invented grid are not surveyed locations of actual towns.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Latitude measures angular position north or south of the Equator. Longitude measures angular position east or west of the Greenwich meridian. Parallels join places of equal latitude; meridians connect the poles. Write latitude first and include the hemisphere. A coordinate without its hemisphere can describe more than one location. Cameroon is in the northern and eastern hemispheres, but classroom points on an invented grid are not surveyed locations of actual towns.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A learner locating a place near Buea first identifies the Equator and the Greenwich reference, then reads north/south and east/west separately. On a graticule, trace the place to the labelled lines. Do not swap a parallel with a meridian just because both appear as straight lines on a flat diagram.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the reference line, read the angle and add the hemisphere. If a point is between marked lines, estimate consistently with the scale. A grid reference based on eastings and northings is a different system from a latitude-longitude coordinate.
